children: Micron Technology Inc. (MU, Financials), the U.S. memory-chip maker supplying the AI boom, is sharing more of its recent success with employees in Taiwan.
The company plans to give engineers there a NT$1 million, or about $31,600, cash bonus along with equity awards.
Entry-level engineers could receive average total compensation of about NT$3.4 million for the past fiscal year after the new awards. That sounds generous. But it has not ended the dispute.

Micron's Taiwan unions are pushing for more, arguing that employees deserve a larger share of the company's record profits. They have also pointed to richer profit-sharing programs at Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix.
Micron and the Taoyuan union did not reach an agreement in last week's mediation, and another round is expected. Taiwan is very important to Micron.

The company has about 15,000 employees there and says it has invested more than NT$1.6 trillion on the island, making the workforce a core part of its manufacturing business. This makes compensation more than a matter of employee relations.

The problem for investors is whether Micron can keep the engineers it needs without letting its labor costs climb too fast. AI has increased the value of those workers, and competitors are competing for many of the same people.

title: Micron Just Made a $32,000 Move as Taiwan Labor Pressure Builds
